title: The Little Prince · Book One
adaptation: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, Le Petit Prince (1943) — 献词与第 1–3 章，原文全文。英文为本项目从法语原文自译。插图为灰盒占位，放在作者原书插图的位置。

passages.text: TO LÉON WERTH
passages.textEn: TO LÉON WERTH

passages.text: I ask the children to forgive me for dedicating this book to a grown-up. I have a serious excuse: this grown-up is the best friend I have in the world.
passages.textEn: I ask the children to forgive me for dedicating this book to a grown-up. I have a serious excuse: this grown-up is the best friend I have in the world.

passages.text: I have another excuse: this grown-up can understand everything, even books for children. I have a third excuse: this grown-up lives in France, where he is hungry and cold.
passages.textEn: I have another excuse: this grown-up can understand everything, even books for children. I have a third excuse: this grown-up lives in France, where he is hungry and cold.

passages.text: He badly needs to be comforted. If all these excuses are not enough, then I will gladly dedicate this book to the child this grown-up once was. All grown-ups were children first.
passages.textEn: He badly needs to be comforted. If all these excuses are not enough, then I will gladly dedicate this book to the child this grown-up once was. All grown-ups were children first.

passages.text: (But few of them remember it.) So I correct my dedication:
passages.textEn: (But few of them remember it.) So I correct my dedication:

passages.text:
TO LÉON WERTH
WHEN HE WAS A LITTLE BOY
passages.textEn:
TO LÉON WERTH
WHEN HE WAS A LITTLE BOY

passages.text: When I was six years old I saw, once, a magnificent picture in a book about the virgin forest called "True Stories." It showed a boa constrictor swallowing a wild beast.
passages.textEn: When I was six years old I saw, once, a magnificent picture in a book about the virgin forest called "True Stories." It showed a boa constrictor swallowing a wild beast.

passages.text: Here is a copy of the drawing.
passages.textEn: Here is a copy of the drawing.

passages.text: The book said: "Boa constrictors swallow their prey whole, without chewing it. After that they cannot move, and they sleep through the six months of their digestion."
passages.textEn: The book said: "Boa constrictors swallow their prey whole, without chewing it. After that they cannot move, and they sleep through the six months of their digestion."

passages.text: I thought a great deal, then, about the adventures of the jungle, and in my turn I managed, with a coloured pencil, to make my first drawing. My Drawing Number One.
passages.textEn: I thought a great deal, then, about the adventures of the jungle, and in my turn I managed, with a coloured pencil, to make my first drawing. My Drawing Number One.

passages.text: It looked like this:
passages.textEn: It looked like this:

passages.text: I showed my masterpiece to the grown-ups and asked them whether my drawing frightened them.
passages.textEn: I showed my masterpiece to the grown-ups and asked them whether my drawing frightened them.

passages.speaker: 大人们
passages.text: They answered: "Why should anyone be frightened by a hat?"
passages.textEn: They answered: "Why should anyone be frightened by a hat?"

passages.text: My drawing was not a picture of a hat. It was a picture of a boa constrictor digesting an elephant.
passages.textEn: My drawing was not a picture of a hat. It was a picture of a boa constrictor digesting an elephant.

passages.text: So I drew the inside of the boa constrictor, so that the grown-ups could understand. They always need things explained. My Drawing Number Two looked like this:
passages.textEn: So I drew the inside of the boa constrictor, so that the grown-ups could understand. They always need things explained. My Drawing Number Two looked like this:

passages.text: The grown-ups advised me to put aside my drawings of boa constrictors, from the outside or the inside, and to take an interest instead in geography, history, arithmetic and grammar.
passages.textEn: The grown-ups advised me to put aside my drawings of boa constrictors, from the outside or the inside, and to take an interest instead in geography, history, arithmetic and grammar.

passages.text: That is how, at the age of six, I gave up a magnificent career as a painter. I had been discouraged by the failure of my Drawing Number One and my Drawing Number Two.
passages.textEn: That is how, at the age of six, I gave up a magnificent career as a painter. I had been discouraged by the failure of my Drawing Number One and my Drawing Number Two.

passages.text: Grown-ups never understand anything by themselves, and it is tiring for children to have to explain things to them, always and always.
passages.textEn: Grown-ups never understand anything by themselves, and it is tiring for children to have to explain things to them, always and always.

passages.text: So I had to choose another profession, and I learned to fly aeroplanes. I have flown a little over all parts of the world.
passages.textEn: So I had to choose another profession, and I learned to fly aeroplanes. I have flown a little over all parts of the world.

passages.text: And geography, it is true, has been very useful to me. At a glance I could tell China from Arizona. That is very handy if you get lost in the night.
passages.textEn: And geography, it is true, has been very useful to me. At a glance I could tell China from Arizona. That is very handy if you get lost in the night.

passages.text: In the course of my life I have had heaps of dealings with heaps of serious people. I have lived a great deal among grown-ups. I have seen them up close.
passages.textEn: In the course of my life I have had heaps of dealings with heaps of serious people. I have lived a great deal among grown-ups. I have seen them up close.

passages.text: It has not much improved my opinion of them.
passages.textEn: It has not much improved my opinion of them.

passages.text: Whenever I met one who seemed to me a little clear-sighted, I tried the experiment of showing him my Drawing Number One, which I have always kept.
passages.textEn: Whenever I met one who seemed to me a little clear-sighted, I tried the experiment of showing him my Drawing Number One, which I have always kept.

passages.text: I wanted to find out whether he was truly a person of understanding. But always the answer came back:
passages.textEn: I wanted to find out whether he was truly a person of understanding. But always the answer came back:

passages.text: "That is a hat." Then I would not talk to him about boa constrictors, or virgin forests, or stars. I would bring myself down to his level.
passages.textEn: "That is a hat." Then I would not talk to him about boa constrictors, or virgin forests, or stars. I would bring myself down to his level.

passages.text: I would talk to him about bridge, and golf, and politics, and neckties. And the grown-up would be very pleased to have met such a sensible man.
passages.textEn: I would talk to him about bridge, and golf, and politics, and neckties. And the grown-up would be very pleased to have met such a sensible man.

passages.text: So I lived alone, with no one I could really talk to, until I had a breakdown in the Sahara Desert, six years ago. Something had broken in my engine.
passages.textEn: So I lived alone, with no one I could really talk to, until I had a breakdown in the Sahara Desert, six years ago. Something had broken in my engine.

passages.text: And since I had with me neither a mechanic nor any passengers, I got ready to attempt, all alone, a difficult repair. For me it was a question of life or death.
passages.textEn: And since I had with me neither a mechanic nor any passengers, I got ready to attempt, all alone, a difficult repair. For me it was a question of life or death.

passages.text: I had barely enough water to drink for eight days.
passages.textEn: I had barely enough water to drink for eight days.

passages.text: So the first night I fell asleep on the sand, a thousand miles from any inhabited land.
passages.textEn: So the first night I fell asleep on the sand, a thousand miles from any inhabited land.

passages.text: I was far more isolated than a shipwrecked sailor on a raft in the middle of the ocean.
passages.textEn: I was far more isolated than a shipwrecked sailor on a raft in the middle of the ocean.

passages.text: So you can imagine my surprise when, at daybreak, I was woken by an odd little voice. It said:
passages.textEn: So you can imagine my surprise when, at daybreak, I was woken by an odd little voice. It said:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Please... draw me a sheep!"
passages.textEn: "Please... draw me a sheep!"

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "What!"
passages.textEn: "What!"

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Draw me a sheep..."
passages.textEn: "Draw me a sheep..."

passages.text: I jumped to my feet as if I had been struck by lightning. I rubbed my eyes hard. I looked hard. And I saw a most extraordinary little fellow, who was studying me gravely.
passages.textEn: I jumped to my feet as if I had been struck by lightning. I rubbed my eyes hard. I looked hard. And I saw a most extraordinary little fellow, who was studying me gravely.

passages.text: Here is the best portrait that, later on, I managed to make of him. But my drawing, of course, is far less charming than its model. That is not my fault.
passages.textEn: Here is the best portrait that, later on, I managed to make of him. But my drawing, of course, is far less charming than its model. That is not my fault.

passages.text: I had been discouraged in my career as a painter by the grown-ups, at the age of six, and I had never learned to draw anything except boa constrictors from the outside and boa constrictors from the inside.
passages.textEn: I had been discouraged in my career as a painter by the grown-ups, at the age of six, and I had never learned to draw anything except boa constrictors from the outside and boa constrictors from the inside.

passages.text: So I stared at this apparition with eyes round with astonishment. Do not forget that I was a thousand miles from any inhabited region.
passages.textEn: So I stared at this apparition with eyes round with astonishment. Do not forget that I was a thousand miles from any inhabited region.

passages.text: And yet my little fellow seemed to be neither lost, nor dying of exhaustion, nor dying of hunger, nor dying of thirst, nor dying of fear.
passages.textEn: And yet my little fellow seemed to be neither lost, nor dying of exhaustion, nor dying of hunger, nor dying of thirst, nor dying of fear.

passages.text: He did not look at all like a child lost in the middle of the desert, a thousand miles from any inhabited region. When at last I managed to speak, I said to him:
passages.textEn: He did not look at all like a child lost in the middle of the desert, a thousand miles from any inhabited region. When at last I managed to speak, I said to him:

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "But what are you doing here?"
passages.textEn: "But what are you doing here?"

passages.text: And he repeated, very softly, as if it were a matter of great seriousness:
passages.textEn: And he repeated, very softly, as if it were a matter of great seriousness:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Please... draw me a sheep..."
passages.textEn: "Please... draw me a sheep..."

passages.text: When a mystery is too overwhelming, one does not dare to disobey.
passages.textEn: When a mystery is too overwhelming, one does not dare to disobey.

passages.text: Absurd as it seemed to me, a thousand miles from any inhabited place and in danger of death, I took a sheet of paper and a fountain pen out of my pocket.
passages.textEn: Absurd as it seemed to me, a thousand miles from any inhabited place and in danger of death, I took a sheet of paper and a fountain pen out of my pocket.

passages.text: But then I remembered that I had mostly studied geography, history, arithmetic and grammar, and I told the little fellow (a little crossly) that I did not know how to draw. He answered:
passages.textEn: But then I remembered that I had mostly studied geography, history, arithmetic and grammar, and I told the little fellow (a little crossly) that I did not know how to draw. He answered:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "That doesn't matter. Draw me a sheep."
passages.textEn: "That doesn't matter. Draw me a sheep."

passages.text: Since I had never drawn a sheep, I drew for him one of the only two drawings I was capable of. The one of the boa constrictor from the outside.
passages.textEn: Since I had never drawn a sheep, I drew for him one of the only two drawings I was capable of. The one of the boa constrictor from the outside.

passages.text: And I was astounded to hear the little fellow answer:
passages.textEn: And I was astounded to hear the little fellow answer:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "No! No! I don't want an elephant inside a boa constrictor. A boa constrictor is very dangerous, and an elephant takes up far too much room. Where I live, everything is very small.
passages.textEn: "No! No! I don't want an elephant inside a boa constrictor. A boa constrictor is very dangerous, and an elephant takes up far too much room. Where I live, everything is very small.

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: I need a sheep. Draw me a sheep."
passages.textEn: I need a sheep. Draw me a sheep."

passages.text: So I drew.
passages.textEn: So I drew.

passages.text: He looked at it closely, and then:
passages.textEn: He looked at it closely, and then:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "No! That one is already very sick. Make me another."
passages.textEn: "No! That one is already very sick. Make me another."

passages.text: I drew:
passages.textEn: I drew:

passages.text: My friend smiled kindly, indulgently:
passages.textEn: My friend smiled kindly, indulgently:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "You can see for yourself... that isn't a sheep, that's a ram. It has horns..."
passages.textEn: "You can see for yourself... that isn't a sheep, that's a ram. It has horns..."

passages.text: So I did my drawing over once more. But it was rejected, like the others:
passages.textEn: So I did my drawing over once more. But it was rejected, like the others:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "That one is too old. I want a sheep that will live a long time."
passages.textEn: "That one is too old. I want a sheep that will live a long time."

passages.text: By then I had run out of patience, since I was in a hurry to start taking my engine apart, so I scribbled this drawing.
passages.textEn: By then I had run out of patience, since I was in a hurry to start taking my engine apart, so I scribbled this drawing.

passages.text: And I tossed off:
passages.textEn: And I tossed off:

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "This is the box. The sheep you want is inside."
passages.textEn: "This is the box. The sheep you want is inside."

passages.text: But I was very surprised to see my young judge's face light up:
passages.textEn: But I was very surprised to see my young judge's face light up:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "That is exactly the way I wanted it! Do you think this sheep will need a great deal of grass?"
passages.textEn: "That is exactly the way I wanted it! Do you think this sheep will need a great deal of grass?"

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "Why?"
passages.textEn: "Why?"

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Because where I live everything is very small..."
passages.textEn: "Because where I live everything is very small..."

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "There will surely be enough. I have given you a very small sheep."
passages.textEn: "There will surely be enough. I have given you a very small sheep."

passages.text: He bent his head over the drawing:
passages.textEn: He bent his head over the drawing:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Not so small as all that... Look! He has gone to sleep..."
passages.textEn: "Not so small as all that... Look! He has gone to sleep..."

passages.text: And that is how I made the acquaintance of the little prince.
passages.textEn: And that is how I made the acquaintance of the little prince.

passages.text: It took me a long time to understand where he came from. The little prince, who asked me a great many questions, never seemed to hear mine.
passages.textEn: It took me a long time to understand where he came from. The little prince, who asked me a great many questions, never seemed to hear mine.

passages.text: It was words spoken by chance that, little by little, revealed everything to me.
passages.textEn: It was words spoken by chance that, little by little, revealed everything to me.

passages.text: So, when he first caught sight of my aeroplane (I shall not draw my aeroplane; that drawing is much too complicated for me), he asked me:
passages.textEn: So, when he first caught sight of my aeroplane (I shall not draw my aeroplane; that drawing is much too complicated for me), he asked me:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "What is that thing?"
passages.textEn: "What is that thing?"

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "It is not a thing. It flies. It is an aeroplane. It is my aeroplane."
passages.textEn: "It is not a thing. It flies. It is an aeroplane. It is my aeroplane."

passages.text: And I was proud to let him know that I could fly. Then he cried out:
passages.textEn: And I was proud to let him know that I could fly. Then he cried out:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "What! You fell out of the sky!"
passages.textEn: "What! You fell out of the sky!"

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "Yes," I said modestly.
passages.textEn: "Yes," I said modestly.

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Oh! That's funny!..."
passages.textEn: "Oh! That's funny!..."

passages.text: And the little prince broke into a very pretty peal of laughter, which annoyed me very much. I like my misfortunes to be taken seriously. Then he added:
passages.textEn: And the little prince broke into a very pretty peal of laughter, which annoyed me very much. I like my misfortunes to be taken seriously. Then he added:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "So you come from the sky too! Which planet are you from?"
passages.textEn: "So you come from the sky too! Which planet are you from?"

passages.text: At once I caught a glimmer of light in the mystery of his presence, and I asked abruptly:
passages.textEn: At once I caught a glimmer of light in the mystery of his presence, and I asked abruptly:

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "Then you come from another planet?"
passages.textEn: "Then you come from another planet?"

passages.text: But he did not answer. He was shaking his head gently, all the while looking at my aeroplane:
passages.textEn: But he did not answer. He was shaking his head gently, all the while looking at my aeroplane:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "It's true that on that, you can't have come from very far away..."
passages.textEn: "It's true that on that, you can't have come from very far away..."

passages.text: And he sank into a reverie that lasted a long time. Then, taking my sheep out of his pocket, he became absorbed in the contemplation of his treasure.
passages.textEn: And he sank into a reverie that lasted a long time. Then, taking my sheep out of his pocket, he became absorbed in the contemplation of his treasure.

passages.text: You can imagine how intrigued I was by this half-confidence about "the other planets." So I did my best to find out more:
passages.textEn: You can imagine how intrigued I was by this half-confidence about "the other planets." So I did my best to find out more:

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "Where do you come from, my little fellow? Where is this 'where I live'? Where do you want to take my sheep?"
passages.textEn: "Where do you come from, my little fellow? Where is this 'where I live'? Where do you want to take my sheep?"

passages.text: After a thoughtful silence he answered:
passages.textEn: After a thoughtful silence he answered:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "The good thing about the box you have given me is that at night he can use it as his house."
passages.textEn: "The good thing about the box you have given me is that at night he can use it as his house."

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "Of course. And if you are good, I will give you a rope as well, to tie him up during the day. And a stake."
passages.textEn: "Of course. And if you are good, I will give you a rope as well, to tie him up during the day. And a stake."

passages.text: The suggestion seemed to shock the little prince:
passages.textEn: The suggestion seemed to shock the little prince:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Tie him up? What a funny idea!"
passages.textEn: "Tie him up? What a funny idea!"

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "But if you don't tie him up, he will wander off anywhere, and he will get lost..."
passages.textEn: "But if you don't tie him up, he will wander off anywhere, and he will get lost..."

passages.text: And my friend burst out laughing again:
passages.textEn: And my friend burst out laughing again:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "But where do you think he would go!"
passages.textEn: "But where do you think he would go!"

passages.speaker: 飞行员
passages.text: "Anywhere. Straight ahead of him..."
passages.textEn: "Anywhere. Straight ahead of him..."

passages.text: Then the little prince remarked gravely:
passages.textEn: Then the little prince remarked gravely:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "That doesn't matter, it's so small where I live!"
passages.textEn: "That doesn't matter, it's so small where I live!"

passages.text: And, with a little melancholy, perhaps, he added:
passages.textEn: And, with a little melancholy, perhaps, he added:

passages.speaker: 小王子
passages.text: "Straight ahead of you, you can't go very far..."
passages.textEn: "Straight ahead of you, you can't go very far..."

effects.note: 献词被作者亲手改写：第二行像墨水一样一笔笔写出来

effects.question: What do you see?
effects.reply: Let's see what the grown-ups said…
effects.note: 延迟判断：先问孩子，不评判，再读大人们的答案

effects.question: Show Drawing Number One to a grown-up near you. What do they see?
effects.note: 亲子共读：轮到孩子测试大人
他的笑声 = 一串小铃铛（第 26 章星星会用同样的笑声）
他从口袋里拿出的，是你画的那只羊
